spans.s:
Śigru is the name of a tribe occurring in the passage of the Rigveda, in which they are mentioned with the Ajas and the Yakṣus as having been defeated by the Tṛtsus and King sudās. It is impossible to say whether they were or were not under the leadership of bheda, as Ludwig plausibly suggests. If Sigru is connected with the later śigru, ‘horse-radish’ (Moringa pterygosperma), which is quite probable, it is possible that the tribe was totemistic and non-Āryan, but this is a mere matter of conjecture. The Matsyas (‘Fishes’) were probably Āryan.
Foot notes vii. 18, 19.
Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 173.
Cf. Oldenberg, Religion des veda, 85; Macdonell, Vedic Mythology, 153; Hopkins, Journal of the American Oriental Society, 16, cliv; Keith, Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society, 1907, 929 et seq.; aitareya Āraṇyaka, 200, n.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 127.
